Notes

Independence is measured in spare bowls, a closed front door and easy sleep. Grand sayings find their ideal environment in a very ordinary bed.

得过且过

得过且过 means muddling through as long as one can, without ambitious plans or a strong sense of purpose. It often carries criticism of that attitude. “One day at a time” sounds gentler in English; the Chinese leaves more room for both deliberate ease and resignation.

  • Lyric text
潇洒自如

潇洒 suggests an unencumbered, stylish ease; 自如 adds being able to act naturally and comfortably. The following insistence that this road was walked by the speaker himself makes the ease an achievement. The song can sound resigned in 得过且过 and proud here without changing its practical aim: retaining control of the scale of one’s life.

  • Lyric transcript
过客

过客 is a traveler passing through a place, extended to someone who occupies only a temporary part of a life. The word redraws the relationship: critics who speak as though they own a stake in the speaker are only visitors. It also makes the earlier “road” image social, with people encountered along it but no obligation to keep traveling together.

  • Lyric transcript
多余的碗筷

碗筷 pairs bowl and chopsticks into a household place setting. Refusing extra company becomes a rule about the table: there is no equipment for an additional guest. The preceding “she” makes the space feel occupied rather than empty. The scene’s comfort depends on keeping an intimate household small, not on proving that the speaker needs absolutely nobody.

  • Genius community transcript
惦记我

惦记 can mean keeping someone fondly in mind, worrying about them, or having one’s eye on something one wants. The surrounding refusal of extra company makes the attention unwelcome. English “thinking of me” preserves the openness of the word without deciding whether these people miss him or want something from him.

  • Lyric text
放下屠刀

The familiar saying continues with becoming a Buddha on the spot: even someone who has done wrong can turn toward good. The lyric stops after laying down the knife, then moves to being at ease and sleeping peacefully. A moral turning point becomes the threshold to an ordinary, restful life.

  • Ministry of Education dictionary: 放下屠刀，立地成佛
  • Lyric text
如鱼得水

如鱼得水 means finding the environment or companion in which one can flourish: the fish finally has its water. The official English title substitutes a duck, an idiomatic choice in English, while the lyric preserves the fish. Here the ideal environment turns out to be a life without interference, with enough security to fall asleep easily.

  • Ministry of Education idiom dictionary: 如魚得水
  • Lyric transcript
轻松入睡

The reward is unusually modest: no anxiety and the ability to sleep. Across the mixtape, sleeplessness, bodily tension and overthinking repeatedly interrupt boasts. This line supplies their quiet opposite. Being at home in one’s life is tested by what the body can do when nobody is watching, rather than by what an audience applauds.

  • Lyric transcript
一年又一年

又 makes recurrence explicit: another year, then another day. Paired with the same sleeping position, time becomes stable repetition instead of progress up a ladder. The intimacy with the pillow gives that repetition warmth. What might look monotonous from outside is presented as a routine safe enough to keep returning to.

  • Lyric transcript
如胶似漆

如胶似漆 compares intimacy to glue and lacquer sticking together; it usually describes people inseparably close. Giving that relationship to a pillow makes the bed a comic partner. After rejecting extra companions and praising ease, the verse finds an attachment that asks for no explanation, no performance and no extra place at the table.

  • Ministry of Education dictionary: 如膠似漆
  • Lyric transcript

About Jackzebra and this mixtape

Zhuang Zhuang Mixtape arrived on Surf Gang on October 2, 2026: 55 tracks, opening with Sour and closing with Sweet. Its cast widens from YoungQueenz on Poker Face to User116, Effie, kuru, yoyi, 春 and 南部犯罪份子. Aghast has a production credit on every track from Hitman through Snatch, giving that stretch a shared collaborator behind its changing scenes.

Surf Gang release · Artist credits

Jackzebra told AVYSS that he writes while singing over a beat he has listened to repeatedly, keeping the images in his head central. He values the room Mandarin leaves for indirect meanings. Listen for ordinary phrases becoming physical scenes: familiarity becomes cooking, authority becomes family seniority, and a tired saying suddenly turns into a threat.

AVYSS interview, 2024

In STATIC, he describes mixtapes as a format for letting ideas flow, reserving an official debut album for later. In a separate conversation about Above & Beyond, he compared that earlier tape to a collection of his producer friends’ work. The credits here likewise reward attention: long-running collaborators sit alongside guests working in Mandarin, Korean and English.

STATIC interview · Sabukaru interview, 2025

The small details connect to his stated interests: he has described playing Temple Run in transit and before shows, watching Top Boy, and wanting to score White Oleander. These give the songs specific points of contact with his life. The notes follow those connections alongside the lyrics’ jokes, invented scenes and competing voices.

His recommendations in Perfectly Imperfect · Dazed interview, 2025 · Interview questionnaire, 2025

Jackzebra has pushed back on being made to represent all of China’s underground. These notes stay close to the words: what an expression usually means, what changes in this line, and how another song answers it. Cultural references have sources; interpretations rest on details you can hear or read in the song.
